text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI
- Moslem Brotherhood decides after seven-hour meeting to boycott parliamentary elections.
- Minister of State for Information Samir Mutawae says Jordanian government rejects extremist Israeli actions like tearing up pages of the Koran and pictures of the Virgin Mary.
- Central Bank to sell 750,000 shares in Housing Bank .
- Father and two sons sentenced to death for murder.
- Jordan and World Food Programme to sign $16 million agreement for land development.
- Eight die in road accident near Iraqi border.
- Bank of Jordan to discuss at extraordinary general assembly tomorrow doubling its capital to 21 million dinars ($29.5 million)
AD-DUSTOUR
- King Hussein to return to Jordan tomorrow from his foreign tour.
- Opinion poll finds 79 percent of Jordanians believe that current election law weakens political participation.
- Head of pro-government National Constitutional Party says holding elections on time is a national necessity.
- Shortage of medical supplies expected because of laboratory refusal to check medicines.
- Egyptian workers get another extension, until August 9, to get their papers in order.
- Housing Bank profits in first six months of 1997 reach 17 million dinars, 26 percent up on the whole of 1996.
AL-ARAB AL-YAWM
- Crown Prince Hassan, returning from Europe, says European investment coming to Jordan soon.
- First Kuwaiti plane to arrive in Jordan today since the 1990 Gulf Crisis.
AL-ASWAQ
- Crown Prince Hassan says U.S., Europe, prepared to help mobilise Jordan's economy.
- Jordan National Bank, Jordan's fourth-biggest bank, follows Central Bank's lead by announcing interest rate cut.
- Tomorrow is deadline for eight international companies to bid to lead manage global share issue of Arab Potash stocks.
JORDAN TIMES
- Top Israeli army official visits Amman in first ever visit to any Arab country.
